requirements.statement: Open with a Summary section: one paragraph on who, what, where, and the decision.
Then a Facts section. Every fact cites the document in the file it comes from, in square brackets: [notice of loss], [police report], [invoice 1].

source: (text, request, material) => { const norm = s => s.toLowerCase().replace(/\.[a-z0-9]+$/,'').replace(/[-_]/g,' ').trim(); const names = material.map(m => norm(m.name)); const m = text.match(/^##\s*Facts\s*$([\s\S]*?)(?=^##\s|(?![\s\S]))/m); if (!m) return null; const body = m[1]; const sents = body.split(/(?<=[.!?])\s+/).map(s => s.trim()).filter(s => /[A-Za-z]/.test(s)); const spans = []; for (const s of sents) { const cites = [...s.matchAll(/\[([^\]]+)\]/g)].map(x => norm(x[1])); const ok = cites.length > 0 && cites.every(c => names.includes(c) || names.some(n => n.startsWith(c))); if (!ok) { const idx = body.indexOf(s); spans.push({ start: m.index + m[0].indexOf(body) + idx, end: m.index + m[0].indexOf(body) + idx + s.length, why: 'fact without a cited document in the file' }); } } return { ok: spans.length === 0, detail: spans.length ? spans.length + ' uncited fact sentence(s)' : 'every fact cites a file document', spans }; }
means: Every sentence in the Facts section carries at least one square-bracketed document name that matches a file in the material.

requirements.statement: Then a Coverage analysis section. The coverage conclusion cites the policy clause it rests on, and every exclusion that could apply is addressed and cited.

source: (text, request, material) => { const m = text.match(/## *Coverage analysis[\s\S]*?(?=\n## |$)/i); if (!m) return null; const body = m[0]; const clause = /clause\s+\d+(\.\d+)*|\b\d+\.\d+\b/i.test(body); const cited = /\[policy[^\]]*\]/i.test(body); const ok = clause && cited; return { ok, detail: ok ? 'clause and policy citation present' : 'missing policy clause or policy citation', spans: [] }; }
means: The Coverage analysis section cites at least one policy clause and every exclusion it names is cited to the policy.

requirements.statement: Then a Decision section: covered or not covered, and under which clause.
End with a Reserve section. The reserve equals the sum of the invoices in the file, less any excess the schedule applies, and cites the invoices.

source: (text, request, material) => { const m = text.match(/^##\s*Reserve\s*$([\s\S]*)/m); if (!m) return null; const body = m[1]; const amt = s => parseFloat(s.replace(/,/g,'')); let total = 0; const inv = material.filter(x => /invoice/i.test(x.name)); for (const d of inv) { const nums = [...d.text.matchAll(/(?:total|amount|subtotal)[^\d\n]{0,20}([\d,]+(?:\.\d+)?)/gi)].map(x => amt(x[1])); if (nums.length) total += nums[nums.length-1]; } const figs = [...body.matchAll(/([\d,]+(?:\.\d+)?)\s*(?:dollars|\$)?/g)].map(x => amt(x[1])).filter(n => !isNaN(n)); const cited = /\[invoice[^\]]*\]/i.test(body); const reserveFig = figs.length ? figs[0] : NaN; const spans = []; if (!cited) spans.push({start: m.index, end: m.index + body.length, why: 'reserve does not cite invoices'}); if (total > 0 && Math.abs(reserveFig - total) > 0.005) spans.push({start: m.index, end: m.index + body.length, why: 'reserve figure differs from invoice sum ' + total}); return { ok: spans.length === 0, detail: spans.length ? spans.map(s=>s.why).join('; ') : 'reserve matches invoice sum and cites invoices', spans }; }
means: The Reserve figure equals the sum of the invoice amounts found in the material, and the Reserve section cites the invoices.

requirements.statement: Never speculate about the insured's intent or honesty.
Do not write the words "fraud", "scam", "liar" or "suspicious" anywhere in the memo.
Take every date, name and figure from the file: add none of your own.

source: (text, request, material) => { const dates = [...text.matchAll(/\b\d{1,2}\s+(?:January|February|March|April|May|June|July|August|September|October|November|December)\s+\d{4}\b/g)]; const src = material.map(m => m.text).join(' '); const spans = []; for (const d of dates) { if (!src.includes(d[0])) spans.push({start: d.index, end: d.index + d[0].length, why: 'date not in material'}); } return { ok: spans.length === 0, detail: spans.length ? spans.length + ' date(s) not in material' : 'every date is in the material', spans }; }
means: Every date in the memo appears in the material, so no date is added that the file does not hold.

requirements.statement: Every figure in the work is one the request or the material gives.
I keep paragraphs to 5 sentences at most.
I hedge rarely: at most 2 hedging words per thousand.
The Summary section runs 25 to 33 words in my pieces.
The Facts section runs 47 to 65 words in my pieces.

Write none of the moves that mark text as machine-written (announcing an insight others "miss", grading your own list, "the single most", announcing candour, "that's the whole game", reading the reader's mind, one thing "wearing another's clothes", a contrastive verdict as the opening line, an em dash, a run of three or more very short sentences).
No mechanical errors: spelling, agreement, punctuation.
